title: Apply for a scientific licence (biodiversity conservation)
summary: This page explains the requirements and steps for applying for a scientific licence under the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016.
intro:
You'll need a licence under the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016 before you undertake an activity for scientific, educational or conservation purposes that is likely to result in one or more of the following:

You'll also need a licence if you plan to:
who_can_apply: You must be undertaking an activity for scientific, educational, or conservation purposes that is likely to result in one or more specified outcomes.
The activity must be conducted in a manner that requires a licence under the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016.
what_you_need: Details of your organisation, employer, or university (including ABN and/or ACN for academic staff and students)
Personal details and contact information for collaborators or staff working independently under the licence
A list of referees who can verify application details
Specific locations for research, including areas in National Parks and Wildlife Service managed lands
Details of the species, populations, or communities that may be affected, and the likely impacts of the project

how_to_steps.text: Log in or create an account.
Follow the prompts to apply for a scientific licence.

faqs.q: What kind of activity requires a scientific licence?
faqs.a: You need a licence if you undertake an activity for scientific, educational, or conservation purposes that is likely to result in one or more specified outcomes.

faqs.q: What information do I need to apply for a scientific licence?
faqs.a: You need your qualifications, details of your organisation or employer, personal details for collaborators, a list of referees, and details about the species and locations affected.

faqs.q: How do I apply for a scientific licence?
faqs.a: You must gather the required information, select the 'Apply online' button, log in or create an account, and follow the prompts.
